title: [Autour de La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois, pages 1 à 67] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting, continued from the previous pages of the 'Longue Marche' notes (§2-type section-conjecture material):
- L/K is a function field.
- U is a smooth model of L/K over K.
- X ⊃ U is a smooth compactification whose boundary D = X∖U = ∪_{i∈I} D_i is a divisor with normal crossings, indexed by the finite set I.
- Π̄_{L/K} is the geometric (profinite) fundamental group, with its Galois extension structure E^{L̄}.
- For x ∈ X∖U, I_x ⊂ Π̄_{L/K} is the inertia subgroup at x, defined up to π-conjugacy. It is (tame part) isomorphic to Ẑ'(1)^{I(x)}, where I(x) = {i | x ∈ D_i}.

The previous page argued as follows. If certain local and global questions (1°, 2°) have positive answers, then a section of E_U over E_K coming from a valuation of L/K with residue field K, and with no centre on U, must normalize a nontrivial subgroup Δ_x ≅ T̂^{I(x)}. That is one of the 'implausible-looking' consequences of the section conjectures.

On this page Grothendieck proposes to study the inertia subgroups I_x more closely. More precisely, he looks at their conjugacy classes as x varies over X∖U. He wants an intrinsic description of these classes, independent of the choice of model X. He remarks this is evident if one accepts what was just said: up to open subgroups (commensurability), they are exactly the inertia groups I_v of valuations v ∈ 𝒳_{L/K} that have no centre in U.

He then sets up the combinatorics of the boundary stratification.
- For J ⊂ I, he defines D_J^* = {x ∈ X | I(x) = J} = ∩_{j∈J} D_j − ∪_{i∈I−J} (Δ_J ∩ D_i), with Δ_J := ∩_{j∈J} D_j. So D_{{i}}^* = D_i ∖ ∪_{j≠i}(D_i ∩ D_j).
- A marginal note changes the notation: D_J will mean the closed stratum ∩_{j∈J} D_j (numbered formula (36)), and the open stratum is {x | I(x)=J}.
- With d = card J, D_J is regular of pure codimension d (possibly empty), by the normal crossings hypothesis.
- He then begins to define a 'simplex' as a subset J ⊂ I with D_J ≠ ∅. The next page completes this: it gives a simplicial structure on I, i.e. the nerve / dual complex of the boundary divisor.

The next page asks for the topological meaning of this complex.
- Its connected components correspond to those of D, and hence to those of the 'punctured tubular neighbourhood at infinity' U_∞ = X̂∖D.
- If the strata were contractible, the complex would compute the homotopy type of U_∞.
- He then writes the local exact sequence T^J → π1(U_J) → π1(D_J) → 1 for the étale localisation along a stratum.

Purpose: to describe the combinatorics of the inertia/'cusp' subgroups at infinity of a higher-dimensional U intrinsically. This is input for analysing which subgroups the sections of the section conjecture must normalize.
errors: No mathematical error. 'D_J regular of codimension d' holds because D has (strict) normal crossings with smooth components D_i. Without strictness (self-intersecting components) the indexing by subsets of I would fail; the hypothesis is implicit.

The claim that I_x is determined intrinsically 'up to open subgroups' as inertia of valuations without centre on U is asserted as evident, conditional on the previous page's presumptions. It is only commensurability information. Valuations of higher rank and non-divisorial valuations are not discussed here.

ideas.what: Inertia subgroups at boundary points of a normal-crossings compactification, considered up to conjugacy and commensurability; intrinsic characterization as inertia groups of valuations of L/K without centre on U
ideas.modern_name: tame inertia / divisorial inertia groups in π1 of the complement of an NCD; valuation-theoretic (birational) characterization of inertia
ideas.usually_credited_to: Abhyankar's lemma; Grothendieck–Murre (tame fundamental group, LNM 208, 1971); later birational anabelian work (Bogomolov, Pop)
ideas.where_published: Grothendieck–Murre, The tame fundamental group of a formal neighbourhood of a divisor with normal crossings on a scheme (LNM 208, 1971); SGA 1 Exp. XIII (Abhyankar's lemma)

ideas.what: Stratification of X by D_J (closed) and D_J^* (open) according to I(x), regular of codimension card J
ideas.modern_name: standard stratification of a strict normal crossings divisor

ideas.what: Simplicial structure on I whose simplices are the J with D_J nonempty, and the question of whether it expresses the homotopy type of the punctured neighbourhood at infinity (completed in the next page)
ideas.modern_name: dual complex / dual intersection complex of the boundary divisor; skeleton of the Berkovich analytification at infinity
ideas.usually_credited_to: Deligne (Théorie de Hodge II, 1971, weight spectral sequence); Danilov (1975); Thuillier (2007); Payne; de Fernex–Kollár–Xu (2017)
ideas.where_published: Not as such in Grothendieck's published texts as far as I know; the dual complex is implicit in the weight filtration work of Deligne (SGA 7 / Hodge II era)

missed.claim: Grothendieck links the dual complex of the boundary NCD to the anabelian problem: the conjugacy classes of inertia/cusp subgroups of the geometric fundamental group of a higher-dimensional U are organized by this complex. He also asks whether the complex encodes the homotopy type of the 'neighbourhood at infinity' U_∞. In later literature, the analogous combinatorial–anabelian use of dual graphs (Mochizuki, Hoshi–Mochizuki combinatorial anabelian geometry) is essentially restricted to curves. Higher-dimensional 'boundary complex as anabelian datum' is less developed, though dual complexes as homotopy invariants of the boundary are well established (Thuillier, Payne, de Fernex–Kollár–Xu). This is a mild, programmatic remark, not a new result.
missed.quote: Si on appelle "simplexe" une partie J ⊂ I [telle que D_J ≠ ∅, on trouve sur I une structure d'ensemble simplicial – quelle est sa signification topologique ?]
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It suggests recovering the boundary dual complex (a known invariant of U by Thuillier/Payne) group-theoretically from the profinite fundamental group plus its inertia data. That is a natural higher-dimensional combinatorial-anabelian question.

deep.surprise_reason: Standard NCD stratification and the dual complex, which Deligne had already used in 1971. The only slightly notable point is that Grothendieck in 1981 explicitly treats the dual complex as an anabelian/homotopical invariant at infinity. This is a programmatic remark without results.
transcription_corrections: Line 3 should read 'l'allure des sous-groupes I_x ⊂ Π̄_{L/K}' (the symbol is crossed/overwritten Π with a bar over it).
In the definition of D_J^*: the removed set is ∪_{i∈I−J} Δ_J ∩ D_i, where Δ_J = ∩_{j∈J} D_j is written under the intersection sign. The stray '{+Δ_J+}' is this label.
'de sorte que D_{{i}} = D_i ∖ ∪_{j≠i}(D_i∩D_j)' is the open stratum D_{{i}}^*.
Left margin likely reads: 'il vaut mieux et décidons de noter D_J comme ∩_{j∈J} D_j (36), et décidons de noter [D_J^*] comme {x ∈ X | I(x) = J}'.

The parenthetical near the top is garbled. It is roughly '(mais ceci est évident, si on admet ce qui vient d'être [suggéré], que ce sont, à sous-groupes ouverts près en plus, les groupes [d'inertie] I_v, pour v ∈ 𝒳_{L/K} n'ayant pas de centre dans U...)'. The duplicated line 'groupes ouverts près en plus, les' is a transcription artifact.
